questions.q: In one line, what does Airbyte do?
options: It builds dashboards and charts for your team
It copies data from apps, databases and files into a warehouse or data lake
It stores your company's files in the cloud
It writes the SQL your analysts run
questions.explain: Think of Airbyte as a data mover. It consolidates data from hundreds of sources into warehouses, lakes and databases, and leaves the reshaping to you afterward.

questions.q: Why does this guide say "self-hostable" instead of "open source" for Airbyte?
options: Airbyte's code is secret and nobody outside can read it
Airbyte charges a fee for every sync you run yourself
You can run it and read the code, but you cannot resell it as a hosted service
Only the paid Cloud version can be installed on your own servers
questions.explain: You can use it free on your own servers and read the source. But the licence (Elastic License 2.0) bars selling Airbyte to others as a hosted service, and the Open Source Initiative does not list it as open source.

questions.q: Your database changes all day. How quickly does Airbyte's change capture pass those changes on?
options: Instantly, as a live stream
In small batches, on a schedule you set (at most every 15 to 60 minutes on Cloud)
Once a month, in one big copy
Only when you press a button every time
questions.explain: Airbyte's own docs say it does not treat change capture as a live stream. It is batch in small steps, so it is a weaker fit if you need changes in seconds (checked Oct 2026).

questions.q: Free to run yourself: what is the catch with Airbyte Core?
options: There is no catch, it costs nothing at all
The software is free, but you pay for the servers and the people who keep it running
It stops working after 30 days
It can only copy a few tables
questions.explain: Free software is not free to run. The bill moves to servers and to the people who upgrade it and fix it at night. Airbyte publishes no figure for that cost.

questions.q: If you want Airbyte to keep your Iceberg tables tidy, what should you do before committing?
options: Nothing, Airbyte's docs say it cleans up old files for you (checked Oct 2026)
Ask who will do the tidy-up work, because the docs do not describe it as a feature
Switch to Cloud, which always includes it
Skip Iceberg, because Airbyte cannot write it
questions.explain: Airbyte can write Iceberg tables, but its page does not describe the clean-up jobs as features. That does not prove it cannot, so ask who owns that work before you commit.
